facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The financial base is a thinly covered, advertising-cyclical broadcaster that is usable for a snapshot only with its definitions kept apart. On issuer Adjusted EBITDA of 709 for the twelve months to June 30, 2026, principal debt of 5,867 is 8.28 times and debt net of cash is 8.03 times. The company's own covenant measure reads 5.73 times on net debt of 5,696 because its denominator is an eight-quarter average of 994 that includes the third and fourth quarters of the 2024 election year and acquisition, synergy and unrestricted-subsidiary adjustments. Both numbers are correct on their own basis; they must not be mixed, and neither is a maintenance test. The one maintenance covenant described is a first lien net leverage limit, which the issuer text ties to revolver borrowings or to more than 50 of uncollateralized letters of credit, with a stated cap of 4.25 times while revolver amounts are outstanding; the issuer reports 2.55 times at June 30, 2026.

facts.text: - Adjusted EBITDA: net income plus depreciation, amortization, non-cash stock compensation, impairments, loss or gain on disposals, interest, early-extinguishment and tax items (S-R-Aug page:12). It is not in any filing and does not add back the 7 and 11 of transaction expenses it reports inside corporate expense. - Leverage Ratio Denominator: eight-quarter average, with acquisitions and divestitures treated as if completed on July 1, 2024, expected synergies, and unrestricted-subsidiary adjustments; some acquisition data is unaudited and un-reviewed (S-Q2-26 page:36). The June 30, 2026 schedule includes "Adjustments for stations acquired or divested, financings and expected synergies during the eight quarter period 144" (S-Q2-26 page:37). - Net debt: the release uses principal less cash (5,691, excluding letters of credit); the covenant schedule adds 5 of letters of credit (5,696). Either excludes the securitization and preferred stock. - LTM here is FY2025 plus six months 2026 less six months 2025; it is not a covenant or pro forma measure.

facts.label: Narrative review
facts.text: - Leverage: on actual earnings, principal debt is 8.28 times Adjusted EBITDA on the last twelve months and 8.67 times in FY2025, against 4.90 times in FY2024. Mechanism: FY2024 carried 497 of political advertising and 1,162 of Adjusted EBITDA; FY2025 carried 42 and 670 while debt rose from 5,690 to 5,810. Implication: the credit is structurally much more levered in off-years than the covenant ratio shows. The covenant total net leverage of 5.73 times uses an eight-quarter average of 994 that still includes 2024 election-year quarters and 144 of acquisition and synergy adjustments, so on the actual LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 709 the same net debt of 5,696 would be 8.03 times (C9). - Coverage: Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest 1.84 times on the last twelve months and interest expense 1.50 times. Mechanism: interest expense is about 473 a year on a weighted coupon near the 7.6% average rate the issuer reports ([S-Q2-26 page:33] "Our average total interest rate was 7.6% and 7.4% during the 2026 and 2025 six-month periods, respectively."); a 10.5% first lien tranche and a 9.625% second lien tranche carry the highest coupons. Implication: little earnings cushion above fixed charges before dividends of 87 and capex of 104. - Cash flow quality: operating cash flow less capex is 146 on the last twelve months, 181 in FY2025 and 608 in FY2024. After preferred and common dividends of 87 it is 59. Mechanism: retransmission consent revenue fell 50 in the first half of 2026 while network affiliation fees fell 61, so net retransmission revenue rose 11. Implication: little free cash for debt reduction without the election-year earnings. - Liquidity: cash plus revolver availability is 921, down from 1,113 at December 31, 2025, after 264 of acquisition spending in the first half. No principal falls due before December 1, 2028, when 739 of term loan and the revolver mature, followed by 1,125 in 2029. The receivables facility of 400 matures March 31, 2028. Implication: the nearest wall is 2028 and refinancing risk concentrates in 2028 to 2031, which is 3,872 or 66.0% of principal. - Data quality: audited annual and unaudited interim statements reconcile on the totals checked (C8, C10, C11). Table text is flattened by extraction; no layout error was found in the rows used. One small inconsistency affects the debt table labels (CP-0 X2 and X3). - Definition risks: Adjusted EBITDA is release-only; the covenant denominator is unaudited in parts; the maintenance covenant text differs between the 10-K and the 10-Q; the credit agreement is not supplied. - Key gaps: the quarter ended September 30, 2026; the revolver draw after July 21, 2026; credit agreement and indentures; the purchase agreements for pending closings; Q3 2025 Adjusted EBITDA is derived, not printed.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Gray Media is the largest owner of top-rated local television stations in the United States by its own description, with stations in 117 full-power markets at August 2026, a Telemundo affiliate group and a small production business. It earns money in three ways: core advertising that follows the economy and the audience, political advertising that arrives in even-numbered years and peaks in the fourth quarter, and retransmission consent fees paid by pay-television distributors, less the fees it pays to the four major networks. In FY2025 retransmission consent was 46% of revenue and core advertising 47%, with political at 1%; in FY2024, an election year, political was 14%. That structure gives the credit two features a creditor must read together: a large, contractual-looking fee stream that is shrinking in subscribers and exposed to blackouts and to network renewals through 2028, and a cyclical advertising stream whose largest swing is political.

facts.text: The transaction story is a station-portfolio reshaping financed with debt and cash. In 2025 the company replaced term loans and unsecured notes with 1,150 of second lien notes and 775 of first lien notes, so that, after the January 2026 repayment of the last 2026 notes, no principal falls due before December 1, 2028. In 2026 it closed purchases from Allen Media Group, Block Communications, Sagamore Hill and Bahakel, swapped three stations to Scripps for two, amended and restated its credit agreement without changing commitments, issued 70 of additional first lien notes, repurchased 50 of preferred stock liquidation value for 30, and completed first closings of the American Spirit Media and WHPM purchases on July 1, 2026. Management says the WBBJ-TV acquisition and other station transactions will contribute to reducing leverage; the filings show the full acquisition cost is already in cash and debt while only part of the earnings is in the last twelve months. The context names no sponsor and the sources describe none: control runs through a dual-class common structure, and a senior preferred stock has a holder the pack does not name.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: In 2025 the company refinanced most of its term loans and its unsecured 2027 notes. On July 18, 2025 it issued 900 of 9.625% senior secured second lien notes due 2032 at par under an indenture of that date, and on December 12, 2025 it added 250 at 102% of par; interest is payable January 15 and July 15. On July 25, 2025 it issued 775 of 7.25% senior secured first lien notes due 2033 at par, payable February 15 and August 15. The second lien proceeds, with 50 borrowed under the revolver, were used to redeem the 2027 notes at par, repay 403 of the 2024 term loan, redeem 125 of the 10.5% first lien notes due 2029 at 103% of par, and pay expenses and for general purposes; the first lien proceeds repaid 630 of the 2021 term loan, 80 of the 2024 term loan and all 50 then drawn under the revolver. The revolver commitment was raised to 750 and extended to December 1, 2028 by the fifth amendment of July 18, 2025. The 2025 refinancing produced a loss on early extinguishment of debt of 10. The result is more secured debt with a later first maturity: second lien notes rank behind the credit agreement and both first lien note series, and all of these benefit from guarantees of substantially all subsidiaries and a pledge of substantially all assets excluding real estate.

First, secured debt grew and unsecured debt fell: first lien and second lien instruments now carry 65.8% of principal against 55.2% at December 31, 2024 (C3). Second, the acquisitions were funded by cash that fell from 368 to 176 and by 70 of first lien debt, while the earnings contribution is only in the months after closing. Third, a debt repurchase program of up to 250 was authorised against liquidity of 921 and a fully drawn receivables facility, and the July repurchase drew on the revolver by an undisclosed amount. The company says "we anticipate that the WBBJ-TV acquisition will contribute to reducing our leverage" ([S-R-Feb page:3]); that is management language about one deal and station transactions announced in the second half of 2025, and no pro forma leverage is supplied.

rows.label: A scaled local television group with revenue split almost evenly between advertising and retransmission fees, a two-year political cycle and 2026 station acquisitions funded by cash and secured debt. Class A shares hold most votes; holders are unidentified.
Retransmission fees were 46% of FY2025 revenue, and network affiliation agreements expire from mid-2027 through December 31, 2028.
Political advertising was 14% of FY2024 revenue and 1% of FY2025, and 2026 is an election year.
The 2025 refinancing added second lien and first lien notes and reduced unsecured debt; 2026 acquisitions were funded with cash and 70 of new first lien notes.
Class A stock carries 10 votes per share, and the Series A preferred stock must be redeemed on certain change of control transactions.
Holders of Class A and of common

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Gray Media is a stretched credit with adequate liquidity: the company has no principal maturity before December 2028, but it carries USD 5,867 million of debt against USD 709 million of last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA. Its strongest support is liquidity of USD 921 million and a maturity profile pushed out by the 2025 refinancing. Its weakest point is earnings coverage: debt is 8.28x Adjusted EBITDA, cash interest cover is 1.84x, and free cash flow after dividends is USD 59 million. What decides the outcome is whether 2026 election-year earnings and the acquired stations lift Adjusted EBITDA toward the USD 994 million denominator the company uses for its covenants, and whether retransmission renewals and the 2028 to 2031 refinancing are managed through the 2027 off-year.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Gray Media's reported covenant leverage of 5.73x total net understates the burden shown by its own earnings. The company's covenant denominator is USD 994 million, an eight-quarter average that includes the third and fourth quarters of the 2024 election year and USD 144 million of acquisition, financing and synergy adjustments; its last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA is USD 709 million, and the same net debt of USD 5,696 million is 8.03x on that figure. Both are correct on their own bases and neither is a maintenance test. The mechanism is that incurrence capacity and covenant optics depend on a smoothed, pro forma denominator while cash interest of USD 385 million is paid out of actual earnings. This is Analyst Interpretation over CP-1 figures.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The company's earnings are cyclical and its fee income is eroding at the same time. Retransmission consent was 46% of FY2025 revenue and political advertising 14% of FY2024 revenue and 1% of FY2025, and USD 133 million of the last twelve months; retransmission consent fell 4% in 2025 and 7% in the first half of 2026 on subscriber loss, one station going independent and a satellite blackout between March and May 1, 2026, with network affiliation fees falling faster so that net retransmission revenue rose to USD 292 million from USD 281 million. Network affiliation agreements expire between mid-2027 and December 31, 2028, just before the December 2028 term loan and revolver maturity. The implication is that FY2026 will flatter cash flow, and FY2027 and FY2028 carry the renewal and refinancing risk.

Network affiliation agreements expire between mid-2027 and December 31, 2028, just before the December 2028 term loan and revolver maturity. The implication is that FY2026 will flatter cash flow, and FY2027 and FY2028 carry the renewal and refinancing risk.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Liquidity is adequate but depleted by the 2026 transactions. Cash fell from USD 368 million to USD 176 million in the first half, after USD 264 million of acquisition spending; revolver availability is USD 745 million; and on July 21, 2026 the company repurchased USD 100 million of 2029 first lien notes and USD 20 million of 2031 notes using cash and an undisclosed revolver draw. Reading two issuer passages together, a first lien net leverage cap of 4.25x applies when the revolver is drawn or more than USD 50 million of letters of credit are uncollateralized; the company reports 2.55x, so a draw outstanding at a quarter-end would activate a test with headroom of about 40% of the denominator (Analyst Interpretation, issuer-described terms only).

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The refinancing in 2025 moved debt up the structure. Principal secured by a lien rose to 65.4% of the total at December 31, 2025 and 65.8% at June 30, 2026, from 55.2% at December 31, 2024, with the 10.5% first lien notes due 2029 and the 9.625% second lien notes due 2032 carrying the highest coupons. Coupon arithmetic gives an annual cost of about USD 443 million on the instruments listed, against an issuer estimate of USD 465 million of interest payments over the next twelve months (the coupon sum excludes receivables-facility interest and fees). The implication for creditors is that unsecured noteholders hold USD 2,008 million behind USD 3,859 million of secured debt, and that the cost of debt leaves little earnings cushion; no recovery conclusion is drawn.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Distributions continue ahead of deleveraging. In the first half of 2026 the company paid USD 17 million of common dividends and USD 27 million of preferred dividends, and it used USD 30 million of new first lien debt to repurchase USD 50 million of preferred liquidation value at a USD 20 million discount. The issuer's USD 465 million interest estimate plus USD 83 million of guided 2026 dividends together equal 77.3% of last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA. Class A shareholders hold 51.5% of the votes and the holders are not identified in the pack, so alignment with creditors cannot be assessed beyond the documented actions.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Gray Media has scale: stations in 117 full-power markets reaching about 37% of US households, with its own count of 78 markets with the top-rated station (Management Language, Nielsen data not verified by the issuer). Its customer and market concentration is low: no advertiser above 5% of broadcast advertising and the largest market, Phoenix, at 5% of revenue (Documentary Fact). Its liquidity is USD 921 million and no principal is due before December 1, 2028, after refinancings that the company says extended maturities beyond the next two political cycles (Documentary Fact; the claim about political cycles is Management Language). The first lien net leverage ratio of 2.55x is well inside the 3.5x incurrence level and the 4.25x cap (Documentary Fact, issuer-reported). The company has reduced debt in the past: USD 520 million of net principal payments in 2024 (Documentary Fact). Net retransmission revenue held at USD 547 million in FY2025 against USD 550 million in FY2024 despite a USD 53 million fall in retransmission fees, because affiliation fees fell USD 50 million (Documentary Fact).

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. Gray Media's leverage is 8.28x on last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA and 8.67x in FY2025, against 4.90x in FY2024, and cash interest cover is 1.84x (Documentary Fact, calculated). Its free cash flow is thin: USD 146 million before and USD 59 million after dividends over the last twelve months (calculated). Its earnings swing with the election cycle and with a high fixed-cost base, and Adjusted EBITDA is a release-only management measure (Documentary Fact). Its revenue base faces subscriber erosion and a cluster of affiliation expiries in 2027 and 2028 (Documentary Fact). A growing share of debt is secured, USD 400 million of receivables financing is fully drawn and outside reported debt, and USD 600 million of senior preferred stock carries a cash dividend of about USD 48 million a year and a change-of-control redemption (Analyst Interpretation over Documentary Facts). Class A shares hold most of the votes and the identities of holders, of the preferred holder and any related parties are not supplied (Insufficient Information). Key legal documents and every figure after June 30, 2026 are missing (Insufficient Information).

spans.text: # CP-0 source readiness: GRAY MEDIA, INC (gtn)
## Request

Issuer: GRAY MEDIA, INC (ticker GTN, NYSE-listed Georgia corporation, Commission File Number 1-13796). As-of date: 2026-11-05. Evidence cutoff: 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit_snapshot, case kind public, run type research. Reporting currency per the run context: USD. Current period per the run context: q2-2026 (quarter ended June 30, 2026). Prior period: fy-2025 (year ended December 31, 2025).

Question answered by this handoff: can the pinned source set support the requested work, and what remains blocked. This handoff gives no credit conclusion, legal interpretation or investment opinion, and it does not normalize, reconcile or calculate figures.

Requested consumers, in run order: CP-1 (financial extraction), CP-1A (business and transaction context), CP-2 (fundamental credit synthesis) and CP-5 (evidence trace validator). The report sections selected for the minimum set are key findings, company operating model, model chart strip, financial and credit metrics, strengths and weaknesses, company profile and transaction summary.

The run context supplies no deal terms, no market quotes, no ratings, no peers, no valuation inputs, no management bridge, no prior case and no portfolio workbook, and it states legal documents as "none". Blank context values (borrower, parent, guarantors, sponsor, market capitalization, net debt, enterprise value) are not treated as zero or as evidence. The context is a user setting, not issuer evidence.
## Sources
### Issuer sources relied on

All seven issuer sources are text extractions (one JSON line per source chunk, cited here as `page:N`, which is the chunk number and not the printed page). The sha256 values below are those of the pinned `.jsonl` files named by the run. The `page:1` text of each file also states a hash of the original HTML filing; that hash is a different value and is not the pin used here.

The pack folder also holds `_retrieval.json`, which the launcher ignored; it is retrieval metadata, not a source, and nothing here relies on it.
### Handoffs supplied
None. CP-0 is the first module in the run, so the request carries no upstream handoff. No handoff hash is listed because none exists.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The filings and earnings releases are sufficient to run the requested snapshot work with bounded limitations. Evidence ends with the August 2026 second-quarter release, and no governing debt documents are supplied. | Medium | No credit agreement or indentures and no third-quarter 2026 report, so covenant terms and post-June liquidity cannot be confirmed. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| The annual report, three quarterly reports and three earnings releases cover statements, debt by instrument, covenant ratios and liquidity in USD millions. | Supports a reported-fact snapshot of the debt stack, liquidity and covenant ratios from primary filings. | High |

| Adjusted EBITDA appears only in the earnings releases, not in any filing; the covenant earnings denominator appears in both. | Earnings-based metrics rest on management-defined figures that no filed schedule corroborates. | Medium |

| Credit agreement, indentures and receivables purchase agreement are not supplied, and the filings describe a March 2026 amendment and restatement of the credit agreement. | Covenant triggers and guarantor terms rest on issuer summaries rather than executed text. | Medium |
| A July 2026 debt repurchase was funded partly by revolver borrowings, and the amount drawn is not disclosed. | June 2026 liquidity does not show the position after the repurchase. | Medium |

| The latest evidence is the August 2026 release; the quarter ended September 2026 is not covered at the November as-of date. | Current leverage and liquidity may differ from the last reported position. | High |
### Readiness view

Source sufficiency is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for all four selected consumers. No consumer is CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED: the issuer identity is unambiguous, every source carries usable located content, and no extraction failure was found. The limitations are bounded and are carried into each consumer below. The assertion is SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY; CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED. This handoff does not assert normalized quarters, reconciliation or downstream input acceptance. A successful text extraction is not a fidelity review, and no fidelity review of tables or figures was done here beyond the spot checks cited.
| Consumer | Source readiness | Located evidence | Carried limitations |

| CP-1 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Audited FY2025 statements and debt note (S-10K page:72 to page:76, page:91 to page:95); interim statements for Q3 2025, Q1 2026 and Q2 2026 (S-Q3-25 page:2, S-Q1-26 page:2, S-Q2-26 page:2 to page:5); leverage schedules in S-10K page:57, S-Q1-26 page:30, S-Q2-26 page:37 | Adjusted EBITDA only in releases; text-only extraction (tables flattened); Q3 2026 absent; covenant ratios are management calculations |

Identity, document class and period were read from the cover pages and body text, not from file names. Confirming quotes:
- [S-10K page:1] "GRAY MEDIA, INC." is the exact registrant name and the report is for "the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025".
- [S-Q2-26 page:1] "For the quarterly period ended June 30, 2026".
- [S-Q1-26 page:1] "For the quarterly period ended March 31, 2026".
- [S-Q3-25 page:1] "For the quarterly period ended September 30, 2025".
- [S-R-Aug page:1] "Gray Media (NYSE: GTN) today announced its financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026."
- [S-R-May page:1] "today announced its financial results for the first quarter that ended March 31, 2026."
- [S-R-Feb page:1] "today announced its financial results for the fourth quarter that ended December 31, 2025."
### Entity, perimeter and instrument roles

The issuer, the reporting registrant and the debt obligor are the same entity, Gray Media, Inc.; no separate borrower or parent is named in the context or in the filings. Guarantor roles as described in the filings:
- [S-Q2-26 page:35] "We are a holding company, and have no material independent assets or operations."

- [S-Q2-26 page:35] "substantially all of our subsidiaries (subject to certain limited exceptions) are joint and several guarantors of, and our ownership interests in those subsidiaries are pledged to collateralize, our obligations under our 2019 Senior Credit Facility, the 2029 1L Notes, the 2033 1L Notes and the 2032 2L Notes."
- [S-Q2-26 page:35] "the 2030 Notes and 2031 Notes have been fully and unconditionally guaranteed, on a joint and several, senior unsecured basis, by substantially all of our subsidiaries"
- [S-Q2-26 page:35] Non-guarantor subsidiaries "are not material or are designated as unrestricted under our 2019 Senior Credit Facility".

The restricted or unrestricted split is not itemized: the covenant schedules show an "Adjustments for unrestricted subsidiaries" line (S-Q2-26 page:37) but no list of unrestricted subsidiaries is supplied. A receivables special purpose vehicle (the SPV) is a separate legal entity: [S-10K page:78] "The SPV is a separate legal entity with its own separate creditors who will be entitled to access the SPV's assets before the assets become available to us."
### Currency, units and periods

The statements state "(in millions)" (for example [S-Q2-26 page:2]) and the run context fixes USD; the sources print no other currency. The context labels the current period q2-2026 and the prior period fy-2025. In the sources these map to the three and six months ended June 30, 2026 (S-Q2-26 page:3) and the year ended December 31, 2025 (S-10K). The balance sheet comparatives are December 31, 2025 in every 2026 interim report. Three period types must stay separate downstream: discrete quarters (three-month columns), year-to-date (six-month and nine-month columns) and the eight-quarter averaged covenant denominator, which [S-Q2-26 page:36] describes as "represents an average amount for the preceding eight quarters then ended."
### Debt, liquidity and covenant evidence located
Debt by instrument at June 30, 2026 is printed in S-Q2-26 page:15, with coupons stated in the note introduction on page:14 and maturities on page:16:
- [S-Q2-26 page:15] "Total outstanding principal, including current portion 5,867"
- [S-Q2-26 page:15] "Borrowing availability under Revolving Credit Facility $ 745 $ 745"
- [S-Q2-26 page:37] "Consolidated Total Net Leverage Ratio (maximum permitted incurrence is 7.00 to 1.00) 5.73"
- [S-Q2-26 page:16] "we were in compliance with all required covenants under all our debt obligations."
- [S-Q2-26 page:34] "we estimate that we will make approximately $465 million in debt interest payments over the twelve months immediately following June 30, 2026."

The annual equivalents are in S-10K page:92 to page:95 (debt table, 2025 refinancing, maturities) and S-10K page:57 (leverage schedule). Quarter-end leverage schedules are in S-Q3-25 page:38 and page:39, S-Q1-26 page:30 and S-Q2-26 page:37; the releases repeat them (S-R-Feb page:12, S-R-May page:10 and page:11, S-R-Aug page:13).
Items outside the debt principal that the sources print and that downstream modules must treat separately:

- Receivables securitization: [S-Q2-26 page:8] "The amount sold to the Purchasers was $400 million as of both June 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025, which was derecognized from the respective condensed consolidated balance sheets." The release debt summary footnote states [S-R-Aug page:4] "Excludes letters of credit, accounts receivable securitization facility and preferred stock."
- Series A Perpetual Preferred Stock is presented outside stockholders' equity (S-Q2-26 page:2, page:3).
- Network affiliation commitments: [S-10K page:61] "Our network affiliation agreements expire at various dates from mid-2027 through December 31, 2028."
- Pension: [S-Q2-26 page:26] "the Pension Plan will be terminated effective October 1, 2026, subject to regulatory approval".

- Litigation: the antitrust consent decree and the consolidated class action are described in S-10K page:109, which states the consent decree "does not subject the parties to any monetary damages or penalties", and [S-Q2-26 page:40] "there have been no additional material legal proceedings or material developments".
### Subsequent events and cutoff

Everything below is dated after the June 30, 2026 balance sheet date and on or before the cutoff. All of it is reported in S-Q2-26 Note 15 and Item 2, or in S-R-Aug; nothing in the pack is dated after August 7, 2026.

- [S-Q2-26 page:25] "On July 21, 2026, we repurchased, in a privately negotiated transaction, $100 million aggregate principal amount of our 2029 IL Notes and $20 million aggregate principal amount of our 2031 Notes" and [S-Q2-26 page:25] "The repurchase was funded using available liquidity, including cash on hand and borrowings under our existing revolving credit facility." The notes text spells the 2029 notes "2029 IL Notes" (typographical); the release names them "10.500% Senior Secured First Lien notes due in 2029" (S-R-Aug page:4).
- [S-Q2-26 page:25] "Securitization Facility. On July 15, 2026, we amended the Securitization Facility to clarify the treatment of receivables from certain customers under bankruptcy proceedings."
- Debt repurchase authorization of up to $250 million through December 31, 2027, approved August 6, 2026 (S-Q2-26 page:26; S-R-Aug page:5).

### Document conflicts and internal inconsistencies

| X1 | Covenant trigger wording differs between the annual report and the latest 10-Q. The 10-K says "(h) maintenance of the First Lien Leverage Ratio while any amount is outstanding under the Revolving Credit Facility". ## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Principal debt of 5,867 is 8.28 times last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA of 709, well above the 5.73 times the company reports on its covenant definition. Liquidity is 921 and no principal matures before 2028. | Medium | Adjusted EBITDA is release-only and last twelve months mixes an election-year half with an off-year half; credit agreement terms and post-June borrowing are not supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Debt over Adjusted EBITDA is 8.28 times on the last twelve months, against 4.90 times in FY2024, when political advertising and EBITDA were far higher. | Leverage on actual earnings is much higher than the covenant ratio; the covenant ratio depends on an eight-quarter average and acquisition add-backs. | Medium |
| Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest 1.84 times on the last twelve months, down from 2.95 times in FY2024. | Thin cover leaves little room for an advertising or retransmission shortfall. | Medium |

| Cash is 176 and revolver availability 745; the receivables facility is fully drawn and there is no maturity before 2028. | No principal falls due before 2028, but July 2026 repurchases were partly funded by revolver borrowings of undisclosed size. | Medium |

| Operating cash flow less capital expenditure is 146 on the last twelve months, and dividends of 87 absorb more than half of it. | Little internally generated cash remains for debt reduction. | Medium |
### Financial base view

The financial base is a thinly covered, advertising-cyclical broadcaster that is usable for a snapshot only with its definitions kept apart. On issuer Adjusted EBITDA of 709 for the twelve months to June 30, 2026, principal debt of 5,867 is 8.28 times and debt net of cash is 8.03 times. The company's own covenant measure reads 5.73 times on net debt of 5,696 because its denominator is an eight-quarter average of 994 that includes the third and fourth quarters of the 2024 election year and acquisition, synergy and unrestricted-subsidiary adjustments. Both numbers are correct on their own basis; they must not be mixed, and neither is a maintenance test. The one maintenance covenant described is a first lien net leverage limit, which the issuer text ties to revolver borrowings or to more than 50 of uncollateralized letters of credit, with a stated cap of 4.25 times while revolver amounts are outstanding; the issuer reports 2.55 times at June 30, 2026.

Three features shape every ratio. First, 2026 is a political on-year: political advertising was 113 in the first half of 2026 against 22 a year earlier, so the last twelve months blend an off-year half with an on-year half and fourth-quarter 2026 will differ from the fourth-quarter 2025 base. Second, 2026 acquisitions add revenue and Adjusted EBITDA only from their closing dates, while the full acquisition cost and the July 2026 funding are already in debt or cash. Third, a 400 receivables securitization is fully drawn and sits outside reported debt principal, as does 600 of Series A perpetual preferred stock at liquidation value. Evidence ends with the August 7, 2026 release; the quarter ended September 30, 2026 is not in the pack.

- Adjusted EBITDA: net income plus depreciation, amortization, non-cash stock compensation, impairments, loss or gain on disposals, interest, early-extinguishment and tax items (S-R-Aug page:12). It is not in any filing and does not add back the 7 and 11 of transaction expenses it reports inside corporate expense.

- Leverage Ratio Denominator: eight-quarter average, with acquisitions and divestitures treated as if completed on July 1, 2024, expected synergies, and unrestricted-subsidiary adjustments; some acquisition data is unaudited and un-reviewed (S-Q2-26 page:36). The June 30, 2026 schedule includes "Adjustments for stations acquired or divested, financings and expected synergies during the eight quarter period 144" (S-Q2-26 page:37).

- Net debt: the release uses principal less cash (5,691, excluding letters of credit); the covenant schedule adds 5 of letters of credit (5,696). Either excludes the securitization and preferred stock.
- LTM here is FY2025 plus six months 2026 less six months 2025; it is not a covenant or pro forma measure.
### Narrative review

- Leverage: on actual earnings, principal debt is 8.28 times Adjusted EBITDA on the last twelve months and 8.67 times in FY2025, against 4.90 times in FY2024. Mechanism: FY2024 carried 497 of political advertising and 1,162 of Adjusted EBITDA; FY2025 carried 42 and 670 while debt rose from 5,690 to 5,810. Implication: the credit is structurally much more levered in off-years than the covenant ratio shows. The covenant total net leverage of 5.73 times uses an eight-quarter average of 994 that still includes 2024 election-year quarters and 144 of acquisition and synergy adjustments, so on the actual LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 709 the same net debt of 5,696 would be 8.03 times (C9).

- Coverage: Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest 1.84 times on the last twelve months and interest expense 1.50 times. Mechanism: interest expense is about 473 a year on a weighted coupon near the 7.6% average rate the issuer reports ([S-Q2-26 page:33] "Our average total interest rate was 7.6% and 7.4% during the 2026 and 2025 six-month periods, respectively."); a 10.5% first lien tranche and a 9.625% second lien tranche carry the highest coupons. Implication: little earnings cushion above fixed charges before dividends of 87 and capex of 104.

- Cash flow quality: operating cash flow less capex is 146 on the last twelve months, 181 in FY2025 and 608 in FY2024. After preferred and common dividends of 87 it is 59. Mechanism: retransmission consent revenue fell 50 in the first half of 2026 while network affiliation fees fell 61, so net retransmission revenue rose 11. Implication: little free cash for debt reduction without the election-year earnings.

- Liquidity: cash plus revolver availability is 921, down from 1,113 at December 31, 2025, after 264 of acquisition spending in the first half. No principal falls due before December 1, 2028, when 739 of term loan and the revolver mature, followed by 1,125 in 2029. The receivables facility of 400 matures March 31, 2028. Implication: the nearest wall is 2028 and refinancing risk concentrates in 2028 to 2031, which is 3,872 or 66.0% of principal.

- Data quality: audited annual and unaudited interim statements reconcile on the totals checked (C8, C10, C11). Table text is flattened by extraction; no layout error was found in the rows used. One small inconsistency affects the debt table labels (CP-0 X2 and X3).

- Definition risks: Adjusted EBITDA is release-only; the covenant denominator is unaudited in parts; the maintenance covenant text differs between the 10-K and the 10-Q; the credit agreement is not supplied.

- Key gaps: the quarter ended September 30, 2026; the revolver draw after July 21, 2026; credit agreement and indentures; the purchase agreements for pending closings; Q3 2025 Adjusted EBITDA is derived, not printed.

Issuer: GRAY MEDIA, INC (ticker GTN), a Georgia corporation headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, listed on the New York Stock Exchange, SIC sector Television Broadcasting Stations, country United States. As-of date: 2026-11-05; evidence cutoff 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit_snapshot. Reporting currency per the run context: USD, amounts in millions unless stated. Current period per the context: q2-2026; prior period fy-2025.

Question: which transaction, business, ownership and operating facts matter most to a creditor, and what do they mean for revenue durability, margin and cash resilience, liquidity, refinancing and creditor control. This handoff gives no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion, and does not score governance. It consumes CP-0 and CP-1 and carries their limitations.

The run context names no sponsor, borrower, parent, guarantor, ratings, quotes or deal terms, and states legal documents as none. Those blanks are not treated as zero or as evidence. Fact rows below carry one of four categories: Documentary Fact (a cited filing states it), Management Language (management's characterisation, quoted and qualified), Analyst Interpretation (my reading of cited evidence) or Insufficient Information (the evidence is missing).

### Business and transaction view

Gray Media is the largest owner of top-rated local television stations in the United States by its own description, with stations in 117 full-power markets at August 2026, a Telemundo affiliate group and a small production business. It earns money in three ways: core advertising that follows the economy and the audience, political advertising that arrives in even-numbered years and peaks in the fourth quarter, and retransmission consent fees paid by pay-television distributors, less the fees it pays to the four major networks. In FY2025 retransmission consent was 46% of revenue and core advertising 47%, with political at 1%; in FY2024, an election year, political was 14%. That structure gives the credit two features a creditor must read together: a large, contractual-looking fee stream that is shrinking in subscribers and exposed to blackouts and to network renewals through 2028, and a cyclical advertising stream whose largest swing is political.

The transaction story is a station-portfolio reshaping financed with debt and cash. In 2025 the company replaced term loans and unsecured notes with 1,150 of second lien notes and 775 of first lien notes, so that, after the January 2026 repayment of the last 2026 notes, no principal falls due before December 1, 2028. In 2026 it closed purchases from Allen Media Group, Block Communications, Sagamore Hill and Bahakel, swapped three stations to Scripps for two, amended and restated its credit agreement without changing commitments, issued 70 of additional first lien notes, repurchased 50 of preferred stock liquidation value for 30, and completed first closings of the American Spirit Media and WHPM purchases on July 1, 2026. Management says the WBBJ-TV acquisition and other station transactions will contribute to reducing leverage; the filings show the full acquisition cost is already in cash and debt while only part of the earnings is in the last twelve months. The context names no sponsor and the sources describe none: control runs through a dual-class common structure, and a senior preferred stock has a holder the pack does not name.

For a creditor the mechanism is straightforward. Political and retransmission revenue drive cash flow; acquisitions and refinancings drive leverage and the secured share of debt; Class A voting control and the preferred stock's change-of-control redemption shape who decides and who is paid first outside the debt. Documents that would show how much of this the creditor group can control, the credit agreement, indentures and purchase agreements, are not in the pack.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

In 2025 the company refinanced most of its term loans and its unsecured 2027 notes. On July 18, 2025 it issued 900 of 9.625% senior secured second lien notes due 2032 at par under an indenture of that date, and on December 12, 2025 it added 250 at 102% of par; interest is payable January 15 and July 15. On July 25, 2025 it issued 775 of 7.25% senior secured first lien notes due 2033 at par, payable February 15 and August 15. The second lien proceeds, with 50 borrowed under the revolver, were used to redeem the 2027 notes at par, repay 403 of the 2024 term loan, redeem 125 of the 10.5% first lien notes due 2029 at 103% of par, and pay expenses and for general purposes; the first lien proceeds repaid 630 of the 2021 term loan, 80 of the 2024 term loan and all 50 then drawn under the revolver. The revolver commitment was raised to 750 and extended to December 1, 2028 by the fifth amendment of July 18, 2025. The 2025 refinancing produced a loss on early extinguishment of debt of 10. The result is more secured debt with a later first maturity: second lien notes rank behind the credit agreement and both first lien note series, and all of these benefit from guarantees of substantially all subsidiaries and a pledge of substantially all assets excluding real estate.

In 2026 the company amended and restated its credit agreement on March 31, 2026 with no change in commitments, term loan principal or stated maturities and no new borrowings, repaid its remaining 2026 notes of 2 on January 20, 2026, and repaid the remaining 10 term loan balance on April 2, 2026. On June 30, 2026 it issued 70 of additional 7.25% first lien notes due 2033 at par in a private placement, using 40 for the first closing of the American Spirit Media purchase on July 1, 2026 and 30 to repurchase 50 of Series A preferred stock liquidation preference. On July 21, 2026 it repurchased 100 of its 2029 first lien notes and 20 of its 2031 notes at par plus accrued interest with cash and revolver borrowings. On August 6, 2026 the board authorized up to 250 of debt repurchases through December 31, 2027. The acquisitions that closed in the first half of 2026 were Bahakel's WBBJ-TV (25, license assets February 13, 2026), the Allen 3 (56, March 27, 2026), the Allen 7 (115, May 1, 2026), Block (80, May 6, 2026) and Sagamore Hill (2, May 8, 2026), plus a non-cash station swap with Scripps on May 15, 2026 recorded at a fair value of 70. The American Spirit Media (anticipated total 50) and WHPM (anticipated total 4) purchases had first closings on July 1, 2026; second closings are subject to regulatory approval and are not assured.

The creditor read-through is mixed and is labelled as analyst interpretation. First, secured debt grew and unsecured debt fell: first lien and second lien instruments now carry 65.8% of principal against 55.2% at December 31, 2024 (C3). Mechanism: new collateralised paper replaced unsecured notes and term loans, so unsecured claims rank behind more secured debt; the second lien tranche is itself junior to 2,709 of first lien debt. Second, the acquisitions were funded by cash that fell from 368 to 176 and by 70 of first lien debt, while the earnings contribution is only in the months after closing. Third, a debt repurchase program of up to 250 was authorised against liquidity of 921 and a fully drawn receivables facility, and the July repurchase drew on the revolver by an undisclosed amount. No sponsor, acquirer or merger is described. The company says "we anticipate that the WBBJ-TV acquisition will contribute to reducing our leverage" ([S-R-Feb page:3]); that is management language about one deal and station transactions announced in the second half of 2025, and no pro forma leverage is supplied.

Legal capacity, willingness and feasibility are kept apart. Capacity: the credit agreement and indentures contain limitations on indebtedness, liens, dividends and repurchases ([S-Q2-26 page:35] "limitations on the payment of dividends and share repurchases"), but baskets are not supplied. Willingness: repurchases and the preferred buyback are documented; no priming or drop-down is. Feasibility: liquidity of 921, a fully drawn receivables facility and 8.28 times leverage on last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA (CP-1) limit how much of the repurchase authorization can be used without drawing the revolver.

spans.text: # CP-2 fundamental credit synthesis: GRAY MEDIA, INC (gtn)
## Request

This handoff gives the fundamental credit view of GRAY MEDIA, INC (ticker GTN) as of 2026-11-05, on the credit_snapshot pathway, in USD, from the accepted source-readiness, financial and business-context handoffs for the period to June 30, 2026 (run period q2-2026, prior period fy-2025). It makes no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.
## Sources
### Issuer sources underlying the upstream handoffs

CP-2 works from the upstream handoffs, not from fresh source text. These are the seven pinned issuer sources those handoffs cite; amounts below are rechecked only against the upstream handoffs and, for the derived figures, against the inputs listed in `## Calculations`.
| Exact source name | sha256 |
| EX-99.1_2026-05-07_ex_956963.htm.jsonl | b04f43ebe7b79436fed34dc07bcf8f9f9fb0c9fac32a39299a3e02ac7ae325d8 |
The run context (sha256 457b491e723cfaa80de6921ac6aa99b1d24251f7cfebd35fd33b60ef8d3cb70e) supplies the currency and period labels only and is not issuer evidence.
### Handoffs supplied
| Module | sha256 | Used for |
| CP-0 | e77a699cb806587c5833b538af86a669d2f7b40e236fe396a25b387c082542af | Source sufficiency, conflicts X1 to X5, gaps G1 to G9; evidence ends August 7, 2026 |
| CP-1 | a5ba76a02d9bf3a11ff3c18cbb17b33ee63a8d295903f868edffbbc7e544712a | Financial figures, leverage, cover, liquidity, debt register, covenants, calculations C1 to C12 |
| CP-1A | 8f6aed0d9aef7292573fab42193a9c269238361033f8ea127bc6b36df2c75a02 | Business model, ownership, transactions, governance behaviour, conflicts K-1 to K-4, calculations C1 to C6 |

Upstream readiness: CP-0 judged the sources ready with limitations; CP-1 and CP-1A each judged CP-2 ready with limitations. Because CP-1A's readiness judgment of this module is not a plain ready, confidence below stays under High. No upstream figure is changed here.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Gray Media is a heavily levered but liquid local broadcaster: principal debt is 8.28 times last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA, interest cover is thin, and no principal falls due before December 2028. | Medium | Governing debt documents, post-June borrowing and the quarter ended September 2026 are not supplied, and Adjusted EBITDA is release-only. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Leverage is 8.28 times on actual earnings against 5.73 times on the covenant definition, whose denominator averages eight quarters. | Covenant headroom overstates earnings capacity; creditors should read leverage on both bases. | Medium |
| Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest 1.84 times, and free cash flow after dividends is 59 on the last twelve months. | Little cash is left to reduce debt without election-year earnings. | Medium |
| Liquidity is 921 and the nearest principal maturity is 739 in December 2028. | The company has time, but 3,872 of principal, 66.0%, matures from 2028 to 2031. | Medium |
| Retransmission fees were 46% of FY2025 revenue and are shrinking, while 2026 political revenue is cyclical. | Earnings quality depends on renewals through 2028 and on the next off-year. | Medium |
### Credit view

Gray Media is a stretched credit with adequate liquidity: the company has no principal maturity before December 2028, but it carries USD 5,867 million of debt against USD 709 million of last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA. Its strongest support is liquidity of USD 921 million and a maturity profile pushed out by the 2025 refinancing. Its weakest point is earnings coverage: debt is 8.28x Adjusted EBITDA, cash interest cover is 1.84x, and free cash flow after dividends is USD 59 million. What decides the outcome is whether 2026 election-year earnings and the acquired stations lift Adjusted EBITDA toward the USD 994 million denominator the company uses for its covenants, and whether retransmission renewals and the 2028 to 2031 refinancing are managed through the 2027 off-year.
### Credit assessment
| Dimension | View | Category | Basis |

| Business risk | Moderate to high: scale and ratings leadership in many markets, no customer above 5% of broadcast advertising, offset by a revenue base in which retransmission fees are 46% of FY2025 revenue and the rest is mostly cyclical advertising, high fixed costs and an election-year cycle | Analyst Interpretation | CP-1A Company and operating model; CP-1 revenue mix |
| Financial risk | High: principal debt 8.28x and net debt 8.03x last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA; cash interest cover 1.84x | Documentary Fact | CP-1 Financials and credit metrics (calculated) |
| Liquidity | Adequate in the near term: USD 921 million of cash and revolver availability; receivables facility fully drawn at USD 400 million | Documentary Fact | CP-1 Liquidity |
| Refinancing | Back-ended: nothing before December 2028, then USD 3,872 million to 2031 | Documentary Fact | CP-1 Chart data: debt maturities |

| Structure and control | More debt is secured (65.8% of principal); Class A holds 51.5% of votes; senior preferred stock outstanding at USD 600 million | Analyst Interpretation | CP-1A Transaction summary, Ownership and control; CP-1 Claims outside debt |
| Overall | Stretched credit with adequate liquidity; confidence Medium | Analyst Interpretation | All of the above; limited by missing legal documents and post-June data |
### Credit thesis

Gray Media can service its debt and has time to refinance, but only if election-year earnings and acquired stations lift Adjusted EBITDA before 2028; on today's last-twelve-months earnings it is a highly levered credit with thin coverage.
### Key findings

Gray Media's reported covenant leverage of 5.73x total net understates the burden shown by its own earnings. The company's covenant denominator is USD 994 million, an eight-quarter average that includes the third and fourth quarters of the 2024 election year and USD 144 million of acquisition, financing and synergy adjustments; its last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA is USD 709 million, and the same net debt of USD 5,696 million is 8.03x on that figure. Both are correct on their own bases and neither is a maintenance test. The mechanism is that incurrence capacity and covenant optics depend on a smoothed, pro forma denominator while cash interest of USD 385 million is paid out of actual earnings. This is Analyst Interpretation over CP-1 figures.

The company's earnings are cyclical and its fee income is eroding at the same time. Retransmission consent was 46% of FY2025 revenue and political advertising 14% of FY2024 revenue and 1% of FY2025, and USD 133 million of the last twelve months; retransmission consent fell 4% in 2025 and 7% in the first half of 2026 on subscriber loss, one station going independent and a satellite blackout between March and May 1, 2026, with network affiliation fees falling faster so that net retransmission revenue rose to USD 292 million from USD 281 million. Network affiliation agreements expire between mid-2027 and December 31, 2028, just before the December 2028 term loan and revolver maturity. The implication is that FY2026 will flatter cash flow, and FY2027 and FY2028 carry the renewal and refinancing risk.

Liquidity is adequate but depleted by the 2026 transactions. Cash fell from USD 368 million to USD 176 million in the first half, after USD 264 million of acquisition spending; revolver availability is USD 745 million; and on July 21, 2026 the company repurchased USD 100 million of 2029 first lien notes and USD 20 million of 2031 notes using cash and an undisclosed revolver draw. Reading two issuer passages together, a first lien net leverage cap of 4.25x applies when the revolver is drawn or more than USD 50 million of letters of credit are uncollateralized; the company reports 2.55x, so a draw outstanding at a quarter-end would activate a test with headroom of about 40% of the denominator (Analyst Interpretation, issuer-described terms only).

The refinancing in 2025 moved debt up the structure. Principal secured by a lien rose to 65.4% of the total at December 31, 2025 and 65.8% at June 30, 2026, from 55.2% at December 31, 2024, with the 10.5% first lien notes due 2029 and the 9.625% second lien notes due 2032 carrying the highest coupons. Coupon arithmetic gives an annual cost of about USD 443 million on the instruments listed, against an issuer estimate of USD 465 million of interest payments over the next twelve months (the coupon sum excludes receivables-facility interest and fees). The implication for creditors is that unsecured noteholders hold USD 2,008 million behind USD 3,859 million of secured debt, and that the cost of debt leaves little earnings cushion; no recovery conclusion is drawn.

Distributions continue ahead of deleveraging. In the first half of 2026 the company paid USD 17 million of common dividends and USD 27 million of preferred dividends, and it used USD 30 million of new first lien debt to repurchase USD 50 million of preferred liquidation value at a USD 20 million discount. The issuer's USD 465 million interest estimate plus USD 83 million of guided 2026 dividends together equal 77.3% of last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA. Class A shareholders hold 51.5% of the votes and the holders are not identified in the pack, so alignment with creditors cannot be assessed beyond the documented actions.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Gray Media has scale: stations in 117 full-power markets reaching about 37% of US households, with its own count of 78 markets with the top-rated station (Management Language, Nielsen data not verified by the issuer). Its customer and market concentration is low: no advertiser above 5% of broadcast advertising and the largest market, Phoenix, at 5% of revenue (Documentary Fact). Its liquidity is USD 921 million and no principal is due before December 1, 2028, after refinancings that the company says extended maturities beyond the next two political cycles (Documentary Fact; the claim about political cycles is Management Language). The first lien net leverage ratio of 2.55x is well inside the 3.5x incurrence level and the 4.25x cap (Documentary Fact, issuer-reported). The company has reduced debt in the past: USD 520 million of net principal payments in 2024 (Documentary Fact). Net retransmission revenue held at USD 547 million in FY2025 against USD 550 million in FY2024 despite a USD 53 million fall in retransmission fees, because affiliation fees fell USD 50 million (Documentary Fact).

Weaknesses. Gray Media's leverage is 8.28x on last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA and 8.67x in FY2025, against 4.90x in FY2024, and cash interest cover is 1.84x (Documentary Fact, calculated). Its free cash flow is thin: USD 146 million before and USD 59 million after dividends over the last twelve months (calculated). Its earnings swing with the election cycle and with a high fixed-cost base, and Adjusted EBITDA is a release-only management measure (Documentary Fact). Its revenue base faces subscriber erosion and a cluster of affiliation expiries in 2027 and 2028 (Documentary Fact). A growing share of debt is secured, USD 400 million of receivables financing is fully drawn and outside reported debt, and USD 600 million of senior preferred stock carries a cash dividend of about USD 48 million a year and a change-of-control redemption (Analyst Interpretation over Documentary Facts). Class A shares hold most of the votes and the identities of holders, of the preferred holder and any related parties are not supplied (Insufficient Information). Key legal documents and every figure after June 30, 2026 are missing (Insufficient Information).
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity | Category |

| Leverage and coverage on actual earnings | Fixed charges of USD 385 million cash interest and USD 87 million of dividends against USD 709 million of Adjusted EBITDA | Little room to absorb a revenue shortfall or fund debt reduction | Material | Documentary Fact (calculated) |

| Election-cycle dependence | Political revenue was USD 497 million in FY2024, USD 42 million in FY2025 and USD 133 million in the last twelve months | Cash flow is strong in even years and weak in odd years; FY2027 is an off-year before the 2028 maturities | Material | Documentary Fact |

| Retransmission erosion and affiliation renewals | Subscriber declines, blackouts and renewal terms through December 31, 2028 | Fee income that looks stable is shrinking; renewal pricing is unseen | Material | Documentary Fact; renewal terms Insufficient Information |

| Refinancing concentration 2028 to 2031 | USD 739 million in 2028, USD 1,125 million in 2029, USD 790 million in 2030, USD 1,218 million in 2031 | USD 3,872 million, 66.0% of principal, must be refinanced in four years | Material | Documentary Fact |

| Rising secured share and structural position | Secured share 65.8% from 55.2%; second lien and first lien notes issued; receivables financing outside debt | Unsecured holders rank behind more secured claims and off-balance-sheet financing | Material | Analyst Interpretation |

| Acquisition execution and funding | USD 332 million of anticipated consideration, of which USD 11 million is pending regulatory approval; funded by cash and USD 70 million of new first lien notes; revolver draw undisclosed | Earnings arrive after the cash leaves; post-June liquidity is unseen | Material | Documentary Fact; draw Insufficient Information |

| Shareholder distributions and control | Common and preferred dividends continue; Class A holds most votes | Cash leaves ahead of debt reduction; alignment with creditors unclear | Minor | Analyst Interpretation |
| Missing legal documents | Credit agreement, indentures and purchase agreements not supplied | Covenant levels and triggers are issuer-described only | Material | Insufficient Information |
## Calculations
All inputs are USD millions or ratios taken from CP-1 or CP-1A as stated; percentages are rounded half up to one decimal and ratios to two decimals.
| ID | Formula | Inputs (upstream source) | Result |

| D1 | Free cash flow to principal debt | LTM operating cash flow less purchases of property and equipment 146 and the same after dividends 59, over principal debt 5,867 (CP-1 C1, C7; Financials and credit metrics) | 2.5%; 1.0% |
| D2 | Cash interest as a share of Adjusted EBITDA | 385 / 709 (CP-1 C1, C5) | 54.3% |

| D3 | Leverage if Adjusted EBITDA returned to the FY2024 level | 5,867 / 1,162; (5,867 − 176) / 1,162 (CP-1 Financials and credit metrics). Illustration of sensitivity to the election cycle, not a forecast; FY2024 included political revenue of 497 | 5.05x; 4.90x |
| D4 | Liquidity to nearest principal maturity | 921 / 739 (CP-1 C3, debt maturities) | 1.25x |
| D5 | Political revenue share, last twelve months | 133 / 3,148 (CP-1 C1) | 4.2% |
| D6 | Covenant versus actual earnings denominators | 994 less 709 (CP-1 C9) | 285 |
| D7 | Acquisition consideration total | Closed in first half 278 + pending 54 = 332 (CP-1A C1) | 332 |

| D9 | Affiliation fees implied by retransmission fees less net retransmission revenue | FY2025 1,429 − 547 = 882 (equal to the 882 in CP-1A); FY2024 1,482 − 550 = 932; changes 1,429 − 1,482 = −53 and 882 − 932 = −50 (CP-1 Revenue mix; CP-1A operating model) | 882 and 932; −53 and −50; net retransmission 547 against 550 |
## Gaps
| Id | Gap | Why it matters and what it affects | Severity | Action |

| P1 | Quarter ended September 30, 2026 not supplied; evidence ends August 7, 2026, 90 days before the as-of date | Leverage, cash and revolver position at the as-of date are unseen; affects every ratio | High | Add the third-quarter 2026 10-Q and release |

| P2 | Revolver borrowing used on and after July 21, 2026 is not disclosed | Post-July liquidity and the maintenance-covenant trigger depend on it | High | Obtain the September 30, 2026 balance sheet |

| P3 | Executed credit agreement, indentures and collateral documents not supplied; 10-K and 10-Q describe the maintenance trigger differently | Covenant levels, baskets and creditor control are issuer-described only | High | Add the documents as amended March 31, 2026 |

| P4 | Adjusted EBITDA exists only in earnings releases; Q3 2025 value derived | The leverage and cover headline rests on a management measure | Medium | Label as release-sourced; use filed GAAP lines alongside |

| P5 | Proxy statement not supplied: holders of Class A, common and Series A preferred and related parties unknown | Control and alignment cannot be assessed beyond voting arithmetic | Medium | Add the 2026 proxy statement |
| P6 | Retransmission and affiliation terms and renewal dates not supplied | Renewal price risk to 2028 cannot be sized | Medium | Obtain contract summaries |

| P7 | No pro forma leverage for the 2026 transactions; last twelve months blends an off-year half and an on-year half | Management's leverage reduction claim cannot be tested; any single-period ratio mislabels the run rate | Medium | Request a pro forma schedule |
| P8 | Conflicts K-1 to K-4 and label differences X2 to X4 unresolved | Dates and small amounts differ between sources | Low | Cite both values |
| P9 | No ratings, quotes, peers or valuation inputs | Not needed for this module; relative value belongs to a later module | Low | None |
## Next module

CP-5 should trace the headline claims of this handoff to their upstream figures: 8.28x and 8.03x leverage, 1.84x cash interest cover, USD 921 million of liquidity, the 5.73x covenant ratio against the USD 994 million denominator, 65.8% secured share and the USD 3,872 million maturity concentration, and should flag the derived items D3 and D6 and the issuer-described covenant terms as lower lineage than the directly sourced figures.
